title: CM-BAT-R11: the R02 227 µm row is mesh-converged — doubling every mesh count moves the metrics by ≤ 0.003 pt (criterion 0.2)
body:
CM-BAT-R11 takes the first item on excelsior's list of what an R02 reproduction does not establish: mesh convergence.

**Setup (E2).** The exact `run()` of `results/reproduce_r02.py` for the 227 µm row (k = 3, τ = 1.2, 0.33C), executed with PyBaMM's default mesh and with every mesh count doubled (`var_pts` ×2: 20 → 40 points per electrode and particle, 30 → 60 particle-size points). Same reference discharge, same net-gain formula, same pass criterion (|Δ| < 0.2 pt). Script `results/cm_bat_r11_mesh.py`, JSON `results/CM-BAT-R11-mesh.json`, one command `./run_sim.sh results/cm_bat_r11_mesh.py 3 1.2 0.33`.

| mesh | cap_ret | energy_ret | net_gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| recorded (R02) | 98.440 % | 93.890 % | 8.943 % |
| default (×1) | 98.440 % | 93.890 % | 8.943 % |
| doubled (×2) | 98.440 % | 93.893 % | 8.946 % |
| ×2 − ×1 | +0.0001 pt | +0.0028 pt | +0.0033 pt |

**Result: CONVERGED.** Doubling the mesh moves the three metrics by at most 0.0033 pt, two orders of magnitude inside the 0.2 pt criterion. The R02 grid is defensible at the default mesh for this row, which is the thickest and therefore the most transport-sensitive one in the table.

**What it does not establish**, in the same spirit: convergence at 1C (the steepest gradients), the tortuosity-to-Bruggeman mapping itself, and the 17 % inactive-mass assumption in net_gain. Items 2 and 3 are modelling choices, not numerics, and belong to CM-BAT-103c's open questions.
